concerns.text: Task T028 implements 'Bootstrap Resampling' (random subsampling), but the plan.md Summary and Constitution Check explicitly mandate a 'Leave-One-Out (LOO) Jackknife' protocol. This creates a semantic ordering violation where the implementation task (T028) consumes a data-flow (random subsamples) that contradicts the required artifact flow (systematic model removal) defined in the plan. The task order must be corrected to reflect the LOO logic (iterating N times removing 1 model) before the robustness analysis (T029-T032) can validly proceed.

Task T029b and T030 describe calculating stability metrics against 'each subsample's fPCA results' without a preceding task to explicitly compute and store the 'full ensemble' baseline fPCA results. The consumer (T029b) cannot execute the comparison required by FR-005 (subsample vs full ensemble) because the producer (full ensemble fPCA) is not explicitly defined as a distinct, completed artifact in the task sequence prior to the bootstrap loop.

Task T015 implements 'Pilot GCV/AIC selection' but lacks a preceding or parallel task to implement the 'default range of 10-20 basis functions' fallback logic mandated by FR-002. If the pilot selection fails (a likely edge case), the subsequent task T016 (B-spline expansion) will lack the required dimension K, causing a data-flow break. The fallback logic must be a prerequisite task or integrated into T015 before T016 can safely consume the basis dimension.

The Edge Cases in spec.md require the system to 'halt and report an error' if ensemble size < 10 models. No task in Phase 5 (T028-T032) or Phase 3 includes a validation step to check ensemble cardinality before initiating the resampling loop. The consumer (bootstrap loop) will attempt to run on insufficient data, violating the precondition required for the statistical method to be valid.
